# Electric circuits

## Circuit quantities

Electric current is the rate at which electric charge flows past a point in a circuit. Voltage is the energy given to each unit of charge by a source such as a battery. Resistance measures how strongly a component opposes the flow of current. Ohm's law states that the current through a conductor is proportional to the voltage across it when the temperature stays constant.

## Series and parallel

In a series circuit the components are connected in one loop, so the same current flows through each of them. In a parallel circuit the components are connected on separate branches, so the voltage across each branch is the same. If one component in a series circuit fails, the whole circuit stops working. Household sockets are wired in parallel so that each appliance receives the full supply voltage.
